narrativeZh: 宇宙最初三分钟便已铸成的第一种原子核——每一个氢核都是 138 亿年前的遗物。你体内每一滴水里，都藏着大爆炸的余温。
narrativeEn: Forged in the first three minutes of the universe: every hydrogen nucleus in your body is a 13.8-billion-year-old relic. Each drop of water carries the afterglow of the Big Bang.

narrativeZh: 大爆炸核合成的主产物，占据宇宙重子质量的四分之一。恒星只是在重复宇宙开端那场炽热的氢聚变。
narrativeEn: The chief product of Big Bang nucleosynthesis, making up a quarter of all baryonic mass. Every star merely repeats the fiery hydrogen fusion the cosmos began with.

narrativeZh: 身世最复杂的轻元素：大爆炸留下了一丝锂-7，但恒星核心会把锂烧掉而非制造它——今天宇宙中的锂，大多由宇宙射线击碎星际碳氧原子核散裂而成，另有部分来自新星与红巨星。本馆与锂的两个「散裂兄弟」铍、硼并列。而理论预测的原初锂比观测多出约三倍，「宇宙锂问题」至今悬而未决。
narrativeEn: The light element with the most tangled pedigree. The Big Bang left a trace of lithium-7, yet stellar cores destroy lithium rather than make it—most lithium today was spalled from interstellar carbon and oxygen by cosmic rays, with contributions from novae and red giants. This exhibit files it beside its spallation siblings beryllium and boron. And the 'cosmological lithium problem'—theory predicts three times more primordial lithium than we observe—remains unsolved.

narrativeZh: 恒星熔炉中无法稳定生成的元素。星际空间里，高速宇宙射线击碎碳氧原子核，碎片便成了铍——一种在近乎真空中诞生的元素。
narrativeEn: No stellar furnace can stably make it. In the void between stars, cosmic rays shatter carbon and oxygen nuclei; the fragments are beryllium—an element born in near-emptiness.

narrativeZh: 硼是宇宙射线散裂的孩子，极其稀有。它在地球上成了硼硅酸盐玻璃和植物细胞壁的关键成分——来自星际碰撞的微小馈赠。
narrativeEn: Boron is a child of cosmic-ray spallation and exceedingly rare. On Earth it stiffens borosilicate glass and plant cell walls—a tiny gift from interstellar collisions.

narrativeZh: 三个氦核在濒死恒星核心碰撞合一，这一「三α过程」造就了碳，也造就了生命的骨架。你是一颗红巨星呼出的碳灰。
narrativeEn: Three helium nuclei fusing in the core of a dying star—the triple-alpha process—made carbon, the skeleton of life. You are carbon ash exhaled by a red giant.

narrativeZh: 在类太阳恒星燃氢的 CNO 循环中累积，随渐近巨星支的恒星风抛入太空。我们呼吸的空气，78% 曾是恒星的燃烧催化剂。
narrativeEn: Accumulated in the CNO cycle of Sun-like stars and blown into space on asymptotic-giant winds. Seventy-eight percent of the air you breathe was once a stellar catalyst.

narrativeZh: 宇宙第三丰富的元素，由大质量恒星核心的氦燃烧铸成，随超新星爆发洒向星际。你每一次呼吸，吸入的都是超新星的遗骸。
narrativeEn: The third most abundant element in the cosmos, forged by helium burning in massive stellar cores and scattered by supernovae. Every breath you take is supernova debris.

narrativeZh: 最活泼的元素，却有着最脆弱的来源：主要在渐近巨星支恒星的氦层间歇燃烧中生成，并以恒星风逃离，才免于被再次烧毁。
narrativeEn: The most reactive element has the most fragile origin: forged mainly in the helium shells of asymptotic-giant-branch stars and swept away on their winds before it can be burned again.

narrativeZh: 大质量恒星碳燃烧阶段的直接产物。城市夜色中的霓虹灯光，正是超新星前身星核心曾经的灰烬在发光。
narrativeEn: A direct product of carbon burning in massive stars. The neon glow of city nights is the ash of a pre-supernova core, lit once more.

narrativeZh: 在大质量恒星碳燃烧壳层中合成。它让海水变咸、让神经冲动传导——每一次心跳都依赖这些超新星粒子。
narrativeEn: Synthesised in the carbon-burning shells of massive stars. It salts the oceans and carries nerve impulses—every heartbeat depends on these supernova particles.

narrativeZh: 碳燃烧与氖燃烧的主产物之一。叶绿素分子中心的那颗镁原子，把超新星的遗产变成了地球上的光合作用。
narrativeEn: A main product of carbon and neon burning. The single magnesium atom at the heart of chlorophyll turns a supernova legacy into photosynthesis on Earth.

narrativeZh: 大质量恒星的氖燃烧铸就。放射性铝-26 在太阳系形成之初加热了小行星——它的 γ 射线今天仍在银河系中勾勒恒星诞生区。
narrativeEn: Forged in neon burning within massive stars. Radioactive aluminium-26 heated the first asteroids; its gamma rays still trace star-forming regions across the Milky Way today.

narrativeZh: 氧燃烧阶段的核心产物，地壳中第二丰富的元素。从岩石到芯片，文明建立在超新星的硅灰之上。
narrativeEn: The core product of oxygen burning and the second most abundant element in Earth's crust. From bedrock to microchips, civilisation stands on supernova silicon ash.

narrativeZh: 在大质量恒星的氖与氧燃烧中稀少地生成。DNA 的骨架与 ATP 的能量货币都依赖磷——宇宙中最稀缺的生命必需元素。
narrativeEn: Made sparingly in the neon and oxygen burning of massive stars. The backbone of DNA and the energy currency ATP both rely on phosphorus—the scarcest of life's essential elements.

narrativeZh: 氧燃烧的产物之一。火山的气息、鸡蛋的味道、蛋白质中的二硫键——都是大质量恒星临终前几天铸成的。
narrativeEn: A product of oxygen burning. The breath of volcanoes, the smell of eggs, the disulfide bonds in your proteins—all were forged in the final days of a massive star.

narrativeZh: 在大质量恒星的氧燃烧壳层中与硅一起合成。它守护着游泳池的清洁，也以盐酸的形式在你的胃里工作。
narrativeEn: Synthesised alongside silicon in the oxygen-burning shells of massive stars. It keeps pools clean and works as hydrochloric acid inside your stomach.

narrativeZh: 氩-36 来自氧与硅燃烧，而地球大气中的氩主要是钾-40 衰变的产物——两种起源在你吸入的每一口空气中交汇。
narrativeEn: Argon-36 comes from oxygen and silicon burning, while most argon in Earth's air is the daughter of potassium-40 decay—two origins mingle in every breath.

narrativeZh: 大质量恒星的氧燃烧壳层铸造。放射性钾-40 至今仍在你体内每秒衰变数千次，是来自超新星的内置时钟。
narrativeEn: Cast in the oxygen-burning shells of massive stars. Radioactive potassium-40 still decays thousands of times each second inside you—a supernova clock built into your body.

narrativeZh: 钙是超新星光谱中最醒目的发射线之一。你的骨骼与牙齿，是大质量恒星氧燃烧与硅燃烧的直接遗产。
narrativeEn: Calcium gives some of the brightest emission lines in supernova spectra. Your bones and teeth are the direct inheritance of oxygen and silicon burning in massive stars.

narrativeZh: 硅燃烧过程中少量生成的过渡金属。钪在宇宙中稀有，却让铝合金轻巧坚韧——航天器与自行车架都受益于此。
narrativeEn: A transition metal made in small amounts during silicon burning. Cosmically rare, scandium makes aluminium alloys light and tough—spacecraft and bicycle frames alike.

narrativeZh: 钛-44 是超新星爆发后的放射性余烬，它的 γ 射线让我们直接「看见」了仙后座 A 超新星遗迹内部的核合成现场。
narrativeEn: Titanium-44 is a radioactive ember of supernovae; its gamma rays let us 'see' nucleosynthesis in action inside the Cassiopeia A supernova remnant.

narrativeZh: 在超新星的不完全硅燃烧中生成。钒让钢更坚韧，也在某些海洋生物的血液中担任氧载体。
narrativeEn: Produced in incomplete silicon burning within supernovae. Vanadium toughens steel and even serves as an oxygen carrier in the blood of certain sea creatures.

narrativeZh: 白矮星热核爆发（Ia 型超新星）的典型产物。不锈钢的光泽与红宝石的红色，都来自一颗被撕碎的恒星残骸。
narrativeEn: A hallmark product of exploding white dwarfs (Type Ia supernovae). The sheen of stainless steel and the red of rubies come from a shredded stellar remnant.

narrativeZh: 锰主要由 Ia 型超新星产出，它与铁的比值是天文学家判断白矮星爆发机制的关键线索。
narrativeEn: Manganese comes mostly from Type Ia supernovae; its ratio to iron is a key clue astronomers use to decode how white dwarfs explode.

narrativeZh: 宇宙中约三分之二的铁来自白矮星的热核爆炸。核聚变到铁为止——它是恒星的终点，也是你血液中氧的载体。
narrativeEn: About two-thirds of the cosmic iron comes from thermonuclear white-dwarf explosions. Fusion stops at iron—the end of a star's life, and the carrier of oxygen in your blood.

narrativeZh: 钴-56 的放射性衰变为超新星提供了持续数月的光芒——我们看到的超新星余晖，其实是钴在发光。
narrativeEn: The radioactive decay of cobalt-56 powers the months-long glow of supernovae—the afterglow we observe is, quite literally, cobalt shining.

narrativeZh: 镍-56 是 Ia 型超新星的首要产物，它的放射性衰变点亮了整场爆炸。一颗白矮星的死亡，约等于半个太阳质量的镍。
narrativeEn: Nickel-56 is the prime product of Type Ia supernovae; its radioactive decay lights up the entire explosion. One white dwarf's death yields about half a solar mass of nickel.

narrativeZh: 弱 s-过程与爆发性核合成在大质量恒星中联合铸成。从青铜器到电线，人类文明的导体来自超新星。
narrativeEn: Made in massive stars by the weak s-process and explosive burning. From bronze vessels to power lines, civilisation's conductor is a supernova product.

narrativeZh: 主要在大质量恒星的爆发与核心坍缩中形成。锌是数百种酶的核心，也是你味觉与免疫的守护者。
narrativeEn: Formed mainly in the explosions and core collapse of massive stars. Zinc anchors hundreds of enzymes and guards your sense of taste and immunity.

narrativeZh: 大质量恒星弱 s-过程的产物。镓在手掌中便会融化，却让蓝光 LED 与高效太阳能电池成为现实。
narrativeEn: A product of the weak s-process in massive stars. Gallium melts in the palm of your hand, yet makes blue LEDs and high-efficiency solar cells possible.

narrativeZh: 大质量恒星氦燃烧核心中的弱 s-过程造就。第一只晶体管由锗制成——信息时代的第一声，来自恒星。
narrativeEn: Made by the weak s-process in the helium-burning cores of massive stars. The first transistor was germanium—the opening note of the information age came from a star.

narrativeZh: 在大质量恒星的爆发与弱 s-过程中生成。砷既是毒药的代名词，也是砷化镓半导体的灵魂。
narrativeEn: Produced in massive-star explosions and the weak s-process. Arsenic is both a byword for poison and the soul of gallium-arsenide semiconductors.

narrativeZh: 来自大质量恒星爆发与中子俘获过程的混合。硒在谷胱甘肽过氧化物酶中守护细胞免受氧化损伤。
narrativeEn: A blend of massive-star explosions and neutron-capture processes. Selenium guards your cells from oxidative damage inside glutathione peroxidase.

narrativeZh: 溴的大部分由快中子俘获过程铸造。它曾在古代的泰尔紫染料中闪耀，如今在阻燃剂与药物中发挥作用。
narrativeEn: Most bromine is forged by rapid neutron capture. It once coloured ancient Tyrian purple; today it serves in flame retardants and medicines.

narrativeZh: 大质量恒星弱 s-过程与爆发核合成的产物。氪-86 的光谱线曾被用来定义「米」——宇宙的尺度由超新星灰烬标定。
narrativeEn: A product of the weak s-process and explosive burning in massive stars. A krypton-86 spectral line once defined the metre—our ruler calibrated by supernova ash.

narrativeZh: 慢中子俘获过程的产物，铷-87 的缓慢衰变成为测定陨石与地球年龄的时钟。
narrativeEn: A product of slow neutron capture; the slow decay of rubidium-87 serves as a clock for dating meteorites and the Earth itself.

narrativeZh: 红巨星深处的慢中子俘获让锶大量产出。它为烟花带来猩红，也为我们骨骼中的钙留下微量伴侣。
narrativeEn: Slow neutron capture deep inside red giants makes strontium abundant. It paints fireworks crimson and rides along with calcium in our bones.

narrativeZh: s-过程的教科书式产物，只有一种稳定同位素钇-89，中子幻数 50 使它在红巨星的中子流中格外稳固。钇铝石榴石激光器与超导体中都有它。
narrativeEn: A textbook s-process product with a single stable isotope, yttrium-89, whose magic neutron number 50 makes it a bottleneck in the red-giant neutron flux. It serves in YAG lasers and high-temperature superconductors.

narrativeZh: 在渐近巨星支恒星大气中，锆与氧结合成氧化锆分子，是天文学家识别富含新造 s-过程元素的「S 型星」的光谱标志。
narrativeEn: In the atmospheres of asymptotic-giant stars, zirconium oxide bands are the spectral signature astronomers use to identify 'S-type' stars rich in freshly made s-process elements.

narrativeZh: 铌只有一种稳定同位素，由 s-过程铸造。它让超导磁体成为可能——粒子加速器与核磁共振成像由此诞生。
narrativeEn: Niobium has a single stable isotope, minted by the s-process. It makes superconducting magnets possible—the heart of particle accelerators and MRI scanners.

narrativeZh: 约一半来自红巨星的慢中子俘获，一半来自爆发事件的快过程。生命中固氮酶的核心正是钼原子。
narrativeEn: Roughly half comes from slow neutron capture in red giants, half from explosive rapid capture. A molybdenum atom sits at the core of nitrogenase, the enzyme that lets life fix nitrogen.

narrativeZh: 第一个人工制造的元素（1937 年）。锝没有稳定同位素，但红巨星光谱中的锝线证明了恒星正在实时制造元素。
narrativeEn: The first element made by humans (1937). Technetium has no stable isotope, yet technetium lines in red-giant spectra proved that stars are making elements right now.

narrativeZh: 主要由 r-过程铸造。钌让硬盘存储密度翻倍，是信息时代隐形的中子星遗产。
narrativeEn: Mainly r-process. Ruthenium doubled hard-drive storage density—a hidden neutron-star legacy of the information age.

narrativeZh: 最稀有的稳定元素之一，几乎全部来自快中子俘获。汽车催化转换器中的铑，每一克都经历过中子星的碰撞。
narrativeEn: One of the rarest stable elements, almost entirely from rapid neutron capture. Every gram of rhodium in a catalytic converter has survived a neutron-star collision.

narrativeZh: r-过程与 s-过程各半。陨石中钯-107 衰变成银-107 的痕迹，记录了太阳系早期行星铁核形成的时间。
narrativeEn: Half r-process, half s-process. The decay of palladium-107 into silver-107, read in iron meteorites, dates the formation of planetary cores in the early Solar System.

narrativeZh: 约四分之三来自快中子俘获。银的光泽曾是货币的化身——一枚银币，是两颗中子星相撞的纪念章。
narrativeEn: About three-quarters from rapid neutron capture. Silver's lustre once embodied money itself—a silver coin is a medal struck by two colliding neutron stars.

narrativeZh: 在濒死恒星的氦层中由 s-过程铸造。镉在地球上有毒，但在恒星光谱里，它是慢中子俘获链的忠实标记。
narrativeEn: Forged by the s-process in the helium shells of dying stars. Toxic on Earth, cadmium is a faithful marker of the slow-neutron-capture chain in stellar spectra.

narrativeZh: 主要来自快中子俘获。铟锡氧化物让每一块触摸屏成为导电的透明窗口。
narrativeEn: Mostly from rapid neutron capture. Indium tin oxide makes every touchscreen a conductive, transparent window.

narrativeZh: 锡拥有十种稳定同位素，比任何元素都多——它的质子幻数 50 使其成为 s-过程路径上的坚固堡垒。青铜时代由它开启。
narrativeEn: Tin has ten stable isotopes, more than any other element; its magic proton number 50 makes it a fortress along the s-process path. It opened the Bronze Age.

narrativeZh: 约三分之二来自 r-过程。锑在古埃及被用作眼影，今天在阻燃剂与半导体中发挥作用。
narrativeEn: About two-thirds r-process. Antimony lined the eyes of ancient Egyptians and now serves in flame retardants and semiconductors.

narrativeZh: 碲在 r-过程峰值附近（中子幻数 82）大量产出，宇宙中的碲比金多得多，却在地壳中极其稀少。
narrativeEn: Tellurium is produced abundantly near the r-process peak at magic neutron number 82—far more common in the cosmos than gold, yet vanishingly rare in Earth's crust.

narrativeZh: 几乎完全来自快中子俘获。你甲状腺中的碘，曾在千分之一秒内于中子星合并的喷射物中被铸成。
narrativeEn: Almost entirely from rapid neutron capture. The iodine in your thyroid was forged in a millisecond inside the ejecta of a neutron-star merger.

narrativeZh: 氙的九种稳定同位素是宇宙化学的罗塞塔石碑，记录了 r-过程、s-过程与早期太阳系放射性衰变的历史。
narrativeEn: Xenon's nine stable isotopes are the Rosetta Stone of cosmochemistry, recording r-process, s-process and early-Solar-System decay histories.

narrativeZh: 主要由快中子俘获铸造。铯原子钟定义了「秒」——时间的标准，由中子星合并的灰烬守护。
narrativeEn: Mainly rapid neutron capture. Caesium atomic clocks define the second—time itself kept by the ash of merging neutron stars.

narrativeZh: s-过程的旗舰元素。富钡恒星是天文学家的活化石：它们的伴星曾在数十亿年前当过红巨星，把新造的重元素「吹」了过来。
narrativeEn: The flagship of the s-process. Barium-rich stars are living fossils: their companions were once red giants that blew freshly minted heavy elements onto them billions of years ago.

narrativeZh: 镧系的门户。在渐近巨星支恒星的热脉冲中由慢中子俘获生成，它为夜视镜与相机镜头带来高折射率玻璃。
narrativeEn: The gateway to the lanthanides. Built by slow neutron capture in the thermal pulses of asymptotic-giant stars, it gives night-vision optics and camera lenses their high-index glass.

narrativeZh: 最丰富的稀土元素，主要来自濒死恒星的 s-过程。它曾是打火石中的火花，今天在催化转换器中净化尾气。
narrativeEn: The most abundant rare earth, mostly s-process from dying stars. Once the spark in lighter flints, today it scrubs exhaust in catalytic converters.

narrativeZh: 镨几乎平分于慢中子俘获与快中子俘获两条途径。焊工与玻璃工匠护目镜中的黄绿色玻璃正是它的颜色。
narrativeEn: Praseodymium is split almost evenly between slow and rapid neutron capture. The yellow-green tint of welders' and glassblowers' goggles is its colour.

narrativeZh: 主要由 s-过程生产。钕磁铁是地球上最强的永磁体，驱动着风力发电机与电动汽车——恒星馈赠的能源基石。
narrativeEn: Mostly s-process. Neodymium magnets are the strongest permanent magnets on Earth, driving wind turbines and electric cars—a stellar gift at the heart of the energy transition.

narrativeZh: 镧系中唯一没有稳定同位素的元素，1945 年在核反应堆裂变产物中被发现。它以盗火的普罗米修斯命名。
narrativeEn: The only lanthanide with no stable isotope, discovered in 1945 among reactor fission products. Named for Prometheus, who stole fire from the gods.

narrativeZh: 约七成来自 r-过程。钐-147 的衰变是测定月球与火星岩石年龄的精准时钟。
narrativeEn: About seventy percent r-process. The decay of samarium-147 is a precise clock for dating rocks from the Moon and Mars.

narrativeZh: r-过程最纯净的示踪元素——约 94% 由快中子俘获产生。天文学家用贫金属星中的铕来追踪银河系早期中子星合并的历史。
narrativeEn: The purest tracer of the r-process—about 94% from rapid neutron capture. Astronomers read europium in ancient stars to chart neutron-star mergers in the early Milky Way.

narrativeZh: 主要来自快中子俘获。钆拥有所有元素中最大的热中子俘获截面，在核磁共振造影剂中让人体组织在影像中发光。
narrativeEn: Mostly rapid neutron capture. Gadolinium has the largest thermal-neutron cross-section of any element and makes tissues glow in MRI contrast scans.

narrativeZh: 几乎全部来自 r-过程。铽的绿色荧光曾点亮阴极射线管电视，今天在节能灯与钞票防伪油墨中闪耀。
narrativeEn: Almost entirely r-process. Terbium's green fluorescence lit CRT televisions and now shines in energy-saving lamps and banknote security inks.

narrativeZh: r-过程铸造。镝让钕磁铁在高温下保持磁性——电动汽车马达中默默工作的中子星灰烬。
narrativeEn: Forged by the r-process. Dysprosium keeps neodymium magnets magnetic at high temperature—neutron-star ash quietly at work inside electric motors.

narrativeZh: 几乎全部来自快中子俘获。钬拥有所有元素中最强的磁矩，用于医疗激光与最强磁铁的极靴。
narrativeEn: Almost all rapid neutron capture. Holmium has the strongest magnetic moment of any element and is used in surgical lasers and the pole pieces of the strongest magnets.

narrativeZh: r-过程铸造。掺铒光纤放大器让光信号跨越海洋——互联网的骨干由中子星合并的产物放大。
narrativeEn: Forged by the r-process. Erbium-doped fibre amplifiers carry light across oceans—the backbone of the internet is boosted by neutron-star merger products.

narrativeZh: 最稀有的稳定镧系元素，几乎完全来自快中子俘获。铥在便携 X 射线源与光纤激光器中工作。
narrativeEn: The rarest stable lanthanide, almost entirely from rapid neutron capture. Thulium powers portable X-ray sources and fibre lasers.

narrativeZh: 镱约三分之二来自 r-过程。镱光晶格钟是当今最精确的时钟之一，每三百亿年误差不到一秒。
narrativeEn: About two-thirds r-process. Ytterbium optical lattice clocks are among the most precise ever built, losing less than a second in thirty billion years.

narrativeZh: 镧系的终点。镥-176 的衰变是测定陨石年龄的时钟；PET 扫描仪的探测晶体也由它制成。
narrativeEn: The end of the lanthanides. Lutetium-176 decay dates meteorites, and lutetium crystals form the detectors in PET scanners.

narrativeZh: 铪与锆几乎难以分离。它主要来自慢中子俘获，用于核反应堆控制棒吞噬中子——一种生于中子的元素，又以吸收中子为业。
narrativeEn: Nearly inseparable from zirconium, hafnium comes mostly from slow neutron capture. It is used in reactor control rods to swallow neutrons—an element born of neutrons that now devours them.

narrativeZh: 约六成来自快中子俘获。钽电容器让手机变得更小，钽-180m 则是自然界最稀有、最长寿的同质异能素。
narrativeEn: About sixty percent rapid neutron capture. Tantalum capacitors shrink smartphones, and tantalum-180m is nature's rarest, longest-lived nuclear isomer.

narrativeZh: s-过程的产物，熔点最高的金属。白炽灯丝曾让钨原子在人类客厅里发光——那是它离开恒星核心之后第二次炽热。
narrativeEn: An s-process product and the metal with the highest melting point. Incandescent filaments once made tungsten glow in living rooms—its second time running hot since leaving a star.

narrativeZh: 几乎全部来自 r-过程。铼-187 的衰变为陨石与地球核心的形成定年；铼合金让喷气发动机叶片耐受极热。
narrativeEn: Almost entirely r-process. Rhenium-187 decay dates meteorites and Earth's core formation; rhenium alloys let jet-engine blades endure extreme heat.

narrativeZh: 密度最大的元素，几乎全部由快中子俘获铸造。锇的同位素记录着地幔与地壳分离的历史。
narrativeEn: The densest element, almost entirely from rapid neutron capture. Osmium isotopes record the history of Earth's mantle and crust separating.

narrativeZh: r-过程的纯粹产物。白垩纪末地层中的铱异常，揭示了 6600 万年前那颗终结恐龙时代的小行星。
narrativeEn: A pure r-process product. The iridium anomaly in the end-Cretaceous clay layer revealed the asteroid that ended the age of dinosaurs 66 million years ago.

narrativeZh: 几乎全部来自中子星合并。2017 年 GW170817 事件中，天文学家估算一次合并便生成了数倍地球质量的铂。
narrativeEn: Almost entirely from merging neutron stars. In the 2017 event GW170817 astronomers estimated a single merger produced several Earth-masses of platinum.

narrativeZh: 金是中子星合并最耀眼的签名。GW170817 的千新星余晖证实：你指上的戒指，诞生于两颗中子星相撞的瞬间。
narrativeEn: Gold is the most dazzling signature of neutron-star mergers. The kilonova glow of GW170817 confirmed it: the ring on your finger was born the instant two neutron stars collided.

narrativeZh: 汞主要诞生于渐近巨星支恒星的慢中子俘获。某些化学特殊星大气中反常高的汞丰度，仍在挑战我们对恒星扩散过程的理解。
narrativeEn: Mercury is mostly born by slow neutron capture in asymptotic-giant stars. Anomalous mercury overabundances in some chemically peculiar stars still challenge our models of stellar diffusion.

narrativeZh: s-过程的末段产物之一。铊-205 的丰度帮助核天体物理学家校准慢中子俘获链在铅附近的终点。
narrativeEn: One of the last stops on the s-process. The abundance of thallium-205 helps nuclear astrophysicists calibrate the end of the slow-capture chain near lead.

narrativeZh: 慢中子俘获的终点站：几乎所有 s-过程链在这里汇集。铅的四种稳定同位素中有三种是铀、钍衰变的终产物——宇宙时钟的最后一格。
narrativeEn: The terminus of slow neutron capture: nearly every s-process chain pools here. Three of lead's four stable isotopes are the end products of uranium and thorium decay—the last tick of cosmic clocks.

narrativeZh: 最重的「稳定」元素——实际半衰期比宇宙年龄长十亿倍。约一半来自 s-过程，它标志着恒星慢中子俘获路径的终结。
narrativeEn: The heaviest 'stable' element—its half-life is a billion times the age of the universe. About half comes from the s-process, marking where the slow-capture path ends.

narrativeZh: 钋没有稳定同位素，自然界中它是铀、钍衰变链的短暂过客——那些铀、钍本身诞生于中子星合并。
narrativeEn: Polonium has no stable isotope; in nature it is a fleeting passenger on the uranium and thorium decay chains—actinides themselves born in neutron-star mergers.

narrativeZh: 地球上最稀有的天然元素，整个地壳中任何时刻仅以克计，作为 r-过程铀的衰变产物瞬息出现又消失。
narrativeEn: The rarest natural element on Earth—only grams exist in the entire crust at any moment—flickering in and out of existence as a decay product of r-process uranium.

narrativeZh: 放射性气体氡，是镭衰变的子代；追根溯源，它来自中子星合并铸造的铀和钍。
narrativeEn: Radon, a radioactive gas, is the daughter of radium's decay; trace its lineage and you arrive at uranium and thorium forged in neutron-star mergers.

narrativeZh: 最不稳定的天然元素，半衰期仅 22 分钟。它存在于锕的衰变链中，源头是 r-过程产生的铀-235。
narrativeEn: The most unstable natural element, with a 22-minute half-life. It lives on the actinium decay chain, descended from r-process uranium-235.

narrativeZh: 居里夫妇从沥青铀矿中提取出的镭，是铀-238 衰变链的中间产物，其祖先铀诞生于中子星合并的烈焰。
narrativeEn: The radium the Curies extracted from pitchblende is a waypoint on the uranium-238 decay chain, whose ancestor was forged in the fire of merging neutron stars.

narrativeZh: 锕系的命名者。它是铀-235 衰变链上的一环——快中子俘获造就的放射性遗产。
narrativeEn: Namesake of the actinides. A link in the uranium-235 decay chain—a radioactive inheritance of rapid neutron capture.

narrativeZh: 钍几乎完全由快中子俘获生成，半衰期 140 亿年。古老恒星光谱中的钍线，是直接丈量宇宙年龄的核时钟。
narrativeEn: Thorium is almost entirely rapid-capture, with a 14-billion-year half-life. Thorium lines in ancient stars are a nuclear clock that directly measures the age of the universe.

narrativeZh: 镤是铀-235 衰变链上的短暂成员。海洋沉积物中的镤-231 是重建古气候与洋流的时间标尺。
narrativeEn: Protactinium is a brief resident of the uranium-235 decay chain. Protactinium-231 in ocean sediments is a yardstick for reconstructing past climate and currents.

narrativeZh: 最重的天然元素，由中子星合并的 r-过程在毫秒间铸成。铀-238 以 45 亿年半衰期为地球定年，也为人类带来了核时代。
narrativeEn: The heaviest natural element, forged in milliseconds by the r-process in neutron-star mergers. Uranium-238's 4.5-billion-year half-life dates the Earth—and ushered in the nuclear age.

narrativeZh: 1940 年在伯克利回旋加速器中诞生的第一个超铀元素。镎以海王星命名——在铀（天王星）之外。
narrativeEn: The first transuranium element, born in Berkeley's cyclotron in 1940. Neptunium is named for Neptune, the planet beyond Uranus.

narrativeZh: 人类制造的最具影响力的元素。钚-238 的衰变热为旅行者号与好奇号提供动力——人造元素驱动星际探索。
narrativeEn: The most consequential element humanity has made. Plutonium-238's decay heat powers Voyager and Curiosity—a human-made element driving exploration of the stars.

narrativeZh: 镅在反应堆中由钚俘获中子生成。几乎每个家庭的烟雾探测器中，都有不到一微克的镅-241 在默默守护。
narrativeEn: Americium forms when plutonium captures neutrons in reactors. Less than a microgram of americium-241 stands guard in nearly every household smoke detector.

narrativeZh: 以居里夫妇命名。锔-244 为火星车的 α 粒子 X 射线光谱仪提供粒子源，帮助分析火星岩石的成分。
narrativeEn: Named for the Curies. Curium-244 provides the particle source for Mars rovers' alpha-particle X-ray spectrometers, revealing the composition of Martian rocks.

narrativeZh: 1949 年于伯克利合成。锫-249 靶材是 2010 年合成第 117 号元素鿬（Ts）的关键原料。
narrativeEn: Synthesised at Berkeley in 1949. Berkelium-249 targets were the crucial ingredient for creating element 117, tennessine, in 2010.

narrativeZh: 锎-252 是强中子源，用于启动核反应堆与探测金银矿藏。它也曾被认为是某些超新星光变曲线的能量来源。
narrativeEn: Californium-252 is a potent neutron source used to start reactors and prospect for gold and silver ores. It was once proposed to power certain supernova light curves.

narrativeZh: 1952 年在第一次氢弹试验「常春藤麦克」的放射性尘埃中发现——人类以毁灭的力量意外铸造了新元素。
narrativeEn: Discovered in 1952 in the fallout of the first hydrogen-bomb test, Ivy Mike—a new element forged by accident in humanity's most destructive act.

narrativeZh: 同样在氢弹尘埃中发现，以费米命名。镄是能以可称量数量制备的最重元素。
narrativeEn: Also found in hydrogen-bomb fallout and named for Fermi. Fermium is the heaviest element that can be produced in weighable amounts.

narrativeZh: 1955 年以每次一个原子的方式合成——第一个「逐原子」发现的元素，以门捷列夫命名，向周期表的缔造者致敬。
narrativeEn: Made in 1955 one atom at a time—the first element discovered atom by atom. Named for Mendeleev, architect of the periodic table.

narrativeZh: 以诺贝尔命名的元素，发现权曾在斯德哥尔摩、伯克利与杜布纳之间争议多年，是冷战科学竞赛的缩影。
narrativeEn: Named for Nobel, its discovery was disputed for years between Stockholm, Berkeley and Dubna—a microcosm of Cold War scientific rivalry.

narrativeZh: 锕系的终点，以回旋加速器之父劳伦斯命名。铹的化学性质暗示相对论效应开始重塑周期表。
narrativeEn: The end of the actinides, named for Lawrence, father of the cyclotron. Its chemistry hints that relativistic effects are beginning to reshape the periodic table.

narrativeZh: 第一个超锕系元素，以卢瑟福命名。𬬻的合成需要用重离子轰击锎靶，每次仅得几个原子。
narrativeEn: The first transactinide, named for Rutherford. Making rutherfordium means bombarding californium targets with heavy ions—a few atoms at a time.

narrativeZh: 以俄罗斯杜布纳联合核研究所命名，纪念冷战时期美苏科学家共同推进的元素竞赛。
narrativeEn: Named for the Joint Institute for Nuclear Research in Dubna, Russia, honouring the Cold War race for new elements shared by American and Soviet scientists.

narrativeZh: 以西博格命名——他在世时便有元素以他命名，史上第一人。𬭳的化学性质已被证实与钨相似。
narrativeEn: Named for Glenn Seaborg—the first person to have an element named after him while still alive. Seaborgium's chemistry has been confirmed to resemble tungsten.

narrativeZh: 以玻尔命名。1981 年在德国达姆施塔特以「冷聚变」技术合成，每个原子仅存在约一秒。
narrativeEn: Named for Niels Bohr. Synthesised in Darmstadt, Germany in 1981 using 'cold fusion' techniques; each atom survives about a second.

narrativeZh: 以德国黑森州命名。𬭶是可以进行化学研究的最重元素之一，其四氧化物的挥发性与锇相似。
narrativeEn: Named for the German state of Hesse. Hassium is one of the heaviest elements whose chemistry has been studied; its tetroxide is volatile like osmium's.

narrativeZh: 以核裂变发现者之一迈特纳命名。鿏极度稀有，至今只合成过几十个原子。
narrativeEn: Named for Lise Meitner, co-discoverer of nuclear fission. Meitnerium is so rare that only a few dozen atoms have ever been made.

narrativeZh: 以德国达姆施塔特命名，1994 年在重离子研究所合成。鐽可能是最重的「铂族」金属。
narrativeEn: Named for Darmstadt, Germany, where it was made in 1994 at the GSI heavy-ion laboratory. Darmstadtium may be the heaviest 'platinum-group' metal.

narrativeZh: 以 X 射线发现者伦琴命名。錀在周期表中位于金之下——理论预测它可能比金更「贵」，也更不稳定。
narrativeEn: Named for Röntgen, discoverer of X-rays. Roentgenium sits below gold in the table—theory predicts it may be even nobler, and far less stable.

narrativeZh: 以哥白尼命名。鎶的实验显示它可能在室温下是气态金属——相对论效应改写了化学常识。
narrativeEn: Named for Copernicus. Experiments suggest copernicium may be a gaseous metal at room temperature—relativistic effects rewriting chemical intuition.

narrativeZh: 日本理化学研究所于 2004 年合成，亚洲首个获得命名权的元素。鿭以「日本」（Nihon）命名。
narrativeEn: Synthesised at RIKEN, Japan in 2004—the first element named in Asia. Nihonium takes its name from 'Nihon', Japan.

narrativeZh: 以俄罗斯弗廖罗夫核反应实验室命名。𫓧靠近理论预言的「稳定岛」，其同位素寿命可达数秒。
narrativeEn: Named for Russia's Flerov Laboratory. Flerovium lies near the predicted 'island of stability'; its isotopes live for several seconds.

narrativeZh: 2003 年在杜布纳合成，以莫斯科州命名。镆的衰变链帮助确认了多个更轻的超重元素。
narrativeEn: Synthesised in Dubna in 2003 and named for Moscow Oblast. Moscovium's decay chains helped confirm several lighter superheavy elements.

narrativeZh: 以美国劳伦斯利弗莫尔国家实验室命名，由美俄团队合作合成。鉝是氧族元素中最重的成员。
narrativeEn: Named for Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, made by a joint US–Russian team. Livermorium is the heaviest member of the oxygen group.

narrativeZh: 2010 年利用锫-249 靶材合成，以美国田纳西州命名。鿬是最新合成的卤素——却可能完全不像卤素。
narrativeEn: Made in 2010 using berkelium-249 targets and named for Tennessee. Tennessine is the newest halogen—yet may behave nothing like one.

narrativeZh: 周期表的尽头。以俄罗斯物理学家奥加涅相命名。鿫是稀有气体族最重的成员，预测在常温下却可能是固体。
narrativeEn: The edge of the periodic table. Named for Russian physicist Yuri Oganessian. Oganesson is the heaviest noble gas—yet predicted to be a solid at room temperature.
